topic: The Windmill Problem (Geometric Rotation & Convex Hulls)
target_audience: High school students interested in competitive mathematics or geometry

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of a Rotating Ray
lecture_lines: A ray rotates clockwise around an anchor.
The ray encounters a point in space.
The anchor switches to the new point.

sections.title: Problem Definition: The Windmill Motion
lecture_lines: Consider points distributed in a plane.
A line pivots around one point.
The line sweeps until it hits another.
animations: Display points randomly on the screen., color #FFFFFF
Draw a line anchored at one point., color #FFFF00

sections.title: Core Mechanism: Angles and Pivot Switching
lecture_lines: The pivot switches to continue rotation.

sections.title: Theorem & Result: The Periodicity
lecture_lines: It completes cycles of finite rotations.
Total turns relate to point permutations.

lecture_lines: This concept aids convex hull algorithms.
The windmill maps the entire plane.
